capabilities: Substitutes {{VAR}} placeholders live in Reading View code blocks
Provides 70+ built-in security variables across 10 categories
Adds custom variables and renameable sections
Copies substituted values via code block copy buttons
Persists values in data.json across restarts
disambiguation: Not a CSS/theming variable tool despite the name; it manages penetration-testing target values substituted into code blocks.
extras: Values, including credentials and hashes, are stored in the plugin's data.json; the README does not mention encryption.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to define reusable target values (IPs, credentials, hashes) that update everywhere they appear, so pentesters must edit every placeholder by hand.
summary: Side panel where penetration testers set target values once; {{VAR}} placeholders in Reading View code blocks are substituted live and copied with real values.
